source.title: On Some Open Problems in Many-Electron Theory

accepted.question_text: For an interacting physical many-electron system with exact ground-state density ρ(r) associated with electron-nuclear attraction potential v(r), does there exist a closed-form expression that gives the ground-state energy Egs in terms of ρ(r) and v(r)?

evidence.quote: For the interacting physical system of interest, assume that one is given the exact ground-state density, ρ(r), associated with electron-nuclear attraction potential v(r). Is there a closed-form expression that gives the ground-state energy, Egs, in terms of ρ(r) and v(r)?
I am not aware of a theorem that states that the answer is definitely no because the system is interacting.

accepted.question_text: For Coulomb many-electron systems, is the ionization energy always greater than the electron affinity? Equivalently, if I[M] denotes the ionization energy of the M-electron system, is there a general proof that I[N + 1] < I[N] for Coulomb systems?

evidence.quote: To my knowledge there is no proof that the ionization energy is always greater than the electron affinity for Coulomb systems, even though this property is so very important in the study of band gaps and strong correlations. In other words, there does not appear to be a general proof that I[N + 1] < I[N] where I[M] is the ionization energy of the M-electron system.
Also, exceptions to I[N + 1] < I[N] have been found for non-Coulomb systems[6].
The property I[N + 1] < I[N] can be proven for certain Coulomb atoms.

accepted.question_text: For a normalized symmetric or anti-symmetric N-particle wave function ΨN with one-particle density ρΨ(x) = N∫|Ψ(x, x2, ..., xN)|² d³x2 ··· d³xN and kinetic energy density TΨ(x) = N∫|∇xΨ(x, x2, ..., xN)|² dx2 ··· dxN, can one find a lower bound for the exchange-correlation energy Exc, defined as the difference between the electron-electron Coulomb expectation and the direct Coulomb energy (1/2)∫ρΨ(x)ρΨ(y)/|x − y| d³x d³y, that involves both TΨ(x) and ρΨ(x)? In particular, can the ratio RΨ(x) = TΨ(x)/[(3/5)(6π²)^(2/3)q^(-2/3)ρΨ(x)^(5/3)], where q is the number of available spin states, be used to improve a Lieb-Oxford-type bound or another lower bound so that the local behavior reduces to Dirac exchange-correlation energy when RΨ(x) is small, while the effective local constant is the Lieb-Oxford constant CLO when RΨ(x) is large?

evidence.quote: The Lieb-Oxford Inequality [7] states that, for any normalized, symmetric or anti-symmetric N-particle wave function, ΨN,

where CLO = 1.68 and ρΨ (x) = N ∫ |Ψ (x, x2, . . . , xN )|2 d3x2 · · ·d3xN (3) is the one-particle density corresponding to ΨN, with ∫ ρΨ (x) d3x = N . The first term on the right side is called the direct energy and the difference between it and the left side of (2) is called the exchange-correlation energy and is denoted by Exc. Thus, (2) gives a lower bound to Exc and the goal is to improve it.

Dirac had shown much earlier [5] that for a free Fermi gas in its lowest energy state, the above inequality would become an asymptotic equality, for large N ≫ 1 by replacing CLO by the spin-dependent constant CD = 0.93 q− 2/3, where q is the number of spin states available to the fermions.
We may define the kinetic energy density as the positive function TΨ (x) = N ∫ |∇ xΨ (x, x2, . . . , xN )|2 dx2 · · ·dxN , (4)

OPEN PROBLEM: Find a lower bound to Exc that involves both TΨ (x) and ρΨ (x) by using the ratio RΨ (x) = TΨ (x) / [(3/5)(6π2)2/3q− 2/3ρΨ (x)5/3] to improve the LO type bound (or some other bound) in a way that (locally) reduces to the Dirac Exc when RΨ (x) is small. When RΨ (x) is large the effective constant (locally) should be CLO.
